channel.title: Caseonix lab notes
channel.description: Research and long-form posts by Srivatsa Kasagar, an AI builder in Waterloo, Ontario.

item.title: Banks told AI agents to stay out. Here is the architecture that lets them back in.
item.description: JPMorgan and Schwab are blocking outside AI agents. The cause is credential sharing. An agent gateway architecture with scoped consent and audit trails.

item.title: Why we built Consul: private wealth intelligence for the people who manage their own money
item.description: The portfolio analysis private banks charge 1% for is mostly deterministic math and plain-language judgment. Consul gives it to anyone with a brokerage account.

item.title: Making six models look like one: a multi-agent orchestration pattern
item.description: How Consul's portfolio briefing runs six model calls in three phases — fan-out, a dependency stage, and streamed synthesis — to read as one assistant.

item.title: Research note — Cheque Image Fraud Detection on AWS
item.description: Lab log exploring an AWS architecture for automated cheque image fraud detection, with the design options and engineering notes.

item.title: Lab note 2/3 — How I improved RAG quality in LocalMind
item.description: Eleven techniques I used to lift RAG quality in LocalMind beyond a naïve baseline — paragraph-aware chunking, table flattening, contextual chunking, BGE asymmetric query prefix, multi-vector query expansion, tuned similarity floor, two-stage LLM reranking, per-document fairness cap, and citation-bound synthesis.

item.title: Lab note 1/3 — LocalMind RAG pipeline
item.description: End-to-end retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline I built for LocalMind on Cloudflare's edge — paragraph-aware chunking, BGE-Small embeddings, contextual chunking, Vectorize ANN search with multi-tenant namespaces, Gemma 4 reranking, and citation-bound generation.

item.title: Lab note 3/3 — The NLP layer alongside LocalMind RAG
item.description: How I built the NLP layer alongside RAG in LocalMind — PIPEDA-aligned layered PII redaction (regex + LLM), hybrid regex and LLM named-entity recognition, table structure recovery for PDF and DOCX, document classification, sentiment with risk flags, and per-document-type review agents — all under JSON-schema constraints.

item.title: Multi-agent Claude Code skills — wealth-guide pattern
item.description: How to structure ambitious Claude Code skills as multi-agent pipelines — parallel dispatch, knowledge grounding, templates, and model routing.

item.title: Extracting T4 data from PDFs in Python (Canada)
item.description: Extracting structured data from Canadian T4 slips with Python — Docling, pydantic-ai, PII handling, audit trails, and the FinLit open-source framework.

item.title: ChatGPT vs self-hosted AI for Canadian law firms
item.description: Comparing ChatGPT and self-hosted AI for Canadian law firms — solicitor-client privilege, CLOUD Act exposure, hallucination risk, sovereign alternatives.

item.title: Building AI tools for PIPEDA — a developer's guide
item.description: A practical guide to building AI tools for PIPEDA, Quebec Law 25, and OSFI B-13 — data residency, consent, CLOUD Act, and Canadian infrastructure patterns.

item.title: AI for Canadian financial services (OSFI E-23 notes)
item.description: Engineering notes on AI in Canadian financial services — OSFI E-23, agentic accountability in AML pilots, and sovereign infrastructure patterns for builders.

item.title: Dug into Pega GenAI Autopilot to figure out what it actually takes to adopt it
item.description: Lab notes on adopting Pega GenAI Autopilot, the App Studio assistant that generates case types, workflows, and data models from natural-language prompts.

item.title: Research note — AuditLM and the AI governance gap
item.description: A working research note on AuditLM — a provider-agnostic governance layer for LLMs in regulated industries. Context, landscape, and what I'm building.

item.title: Research note — NordID and Canadian business identity infrastructure
item.description: A working research note on NordID — the data and intelligence layer under every Canadian KYB stack. Registry, tax, UBO, sanctions, and FINTRAC-rule-cited decisions through one API.
